action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
The game is a standard 6x7 Connect 4 (Connect X where X=4). The first player, 'x', has opened the game by placing their piece in the center column (column 3). In Connect 4, the center column is the most strategically vital column because it belongs to the most possible winning lines (horizontal, vertical, and diagonal). 

According to game theory and perfect play analysis for Connect 4, the optimal response for the second player, 'o', after the first player has taken the bottom spot in the center column, is to also play in the center column. This move blocks player 'x' from building a vertical line in the most important column and establishes 'o's own presence in the center. Any other move (such as playing in columns 2 or 4) allows player 'x' to exert more control over the center and results in a faster theoretical win for the first player. By playing in column 3, player 'o' minimizes the advantage held by the first player.

Final Answer: 3

action.thoughts:
Reasoning:
1. There is no immediate winning move for either side – every column still leaves both players at most two in-a-row.
2. The best strategic policy in Connect-4 is to occupy the centre of the board and to build a low (bottom–row) horizontal chain that can later branch into multiple threats.
3. We already own the centre bottom cell (row 5, col 3).  
   Our next priority is therefore to extend that bottom-row foothold into the adjacent column, giving us the beginnings of a 3- or 4-long horizontal string while keeping the piece as low as possible (low pieces are always more valuable because nothing can later be dropped beneath them).
4. Dropping in column 2 (row 5, col 2) achieves exactly this:
   • it puts two adjacent x’s on the bottom row (cols 2 and 3);  
   • it keeps the move in one of the three central columns (2-3-4);  
   • it does not give the opponent any immediate counter-threat – the only reply that looks attractive for o is to stack on top of our new disk in column 2, which still leaves us free to continue building either horizontally (into column 4) or diagonally.

5. Playing again in column 3 would place an x above o, but the o already breaks the vertical, so that move scores lower.  
   Playing in column 4 is symmetrical to column 2 but is slightly inferior because it allows o to create two adjoining o’s on row 4 (cols 3 and 4) immediately; column 2 keeps o confined to the left side, where we already control the bottom square.

Hence the optimal move is to drop in column 2.
